definitions.gloss: act, deed, doing, work (usually negative or mischievous)
definitions.explanation: An action or deed, almost always used to attribute blame or responsibility for something bad or mischievous.

examples.english: Who did this? (Whose doing is this?)
The garden was probably messed up by a cat.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{事件|じけん}→事件：01568_jiken⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{犯罪|はんざい}{組織|そしき}→犯罪組織：26956_hanzaisoshiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{仕業|しわざ}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{警察|けいさつ}→警察：01393_keisatsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{見|み}ている→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: The police believe this incident is the work of a criminal organization.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{仕業|しわざ}だ: it's the doing of ...
- ⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{仕業|しわざ}: whose doing
- ⟦{犯人|はんにん}→犯人：03572_hannin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{仕業|しわざ}: the criminal's doing

USAGE: Almost exclusively used in negative contexts — mischief, crime, damage, or blame. Rarely used for positive actions. Common in mystery stories, news reports, and when attributing blame.

NOTE: Can also be used humorously for minor mischief: ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{消|き}えた→消える：02520_kieru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{仕業|しわざ}だ (The disappearing sweets were the children's doing).
